1. Edit edge 4 to nor_conv_3x3, conditioned on edge 0 being nor_conv_3x3. With a conv upstream, edge 4 extends a deep path, adding receptive field and capacity, so the gain is higher.
2. Edit edge 5 to nor_conv_3x3, conditioned on edge 2 being nor_conv_3x3. A deeper 0→1→2→3 conv chain is stronger, so the gain is higher. The alternative, redundancy, seems less likely.
3. Edit edge 0 to nor_conv_3x3, conditioned on edge 0 currently being skip_connect. Replacing a skip with a conv on the shared first edge gives a smaller gain than replacing none, because skip already carries the signal while none leaves the path dead. So the gain is lower than for the none-replacing case.
4. Edit edge 3 to nor_conv_3x3, conditioned on edge 3 being skip_connect. The direct 0→3 edge is already a good residual path, so converting it adds little, and the gain is lower than when it was none.
5. Edit edge 1 to nor_conv_3x3, conditioned on edge 1 being avg_pool_3x3. Replacing pool with conv gives a large gain because pooling is a weak feature extractor, so the gain is higher.
6. Edit edge 4 to nor_conv_3x3, conditioned on edge 3 being avg_pool_3x3. Pool on the parallel edge into node 3 offers little learned capacity, so the conv adds more. The gain is higher than when edge 3 is skip, which already gives a clean shortcut.
7. Edit edge 2 to nor_conv_1x1, conditioned on edge 1 being skip_connect. A skip on the parallel path already supplies gradient flow, so the extra conv is less necessary and the gain is lower.
8. Edit edge 3 to none, conditioned on edge 5 being nor_conv_3x3. A conv alternative path into node 3 compensates for the lost direct edge, so the loss is smaller. That means the effect is higher than when edge 5 is a parameter-free op.
9. Edit edge 1 to none, conditioned on edge 2 being nor_conv_3x3. The route 0→1→2 with a conv compensates for capacity, so the loss is smaller (higher effect).
10. Edit edge 5 to none, conditioned on edge 4 being avg_pool_3x3. The pooling alternative cannot compensate for capacity, so removing edge 5 hurts more (lower effect).
